reading: Mogging has been named word of the year by the Collins English Dictionary.
The informal term describes outshining someone, especially by looking more attractive than they do.
It is popular with Generations Z and Alpha, both online and in everyday conversation.
Its usage increased by 210% as it became mainstream in 2026.
Depending on the context, people can use it as either a compliment or a playful put-down.
Collins' managing director Alex Beecroft explained that language experts study how often words appear and examine patterns in their use.
He said the selection shows how each generation influences language.
Collins uses a range of sources, including social media, to follow changes in English in the UK.
The shortlist also included ghost job, an advertised position that an employer has no intention of filling.
In 2025, Collins selected vibe coding, which means creating an app or website by describing it to artificial intelligence.
